title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, Status & Customer Comms
author: Ava Chen
body:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response standards: the incident lifecycle, runbook patterns, postmortem requirements, on-call rotations and escalation, game day planning, and templates for status page and customer communications. It is the canonical reference for engineers, SREs, and support on how to detect, respond, communicate, and learn from incidents affecting hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

1) Goals and scope
- Goal: Restore customer-visible service within SLOs while minimizing blast radius and maximizing clear communications.
- Scope: Tier-0/Tier-1 customer-impacting incidents (hosted API outages, Dedicated capacity degradation, Private deployment control-plane failures) and operational incidents that affect inference correctness, latency, or availability.

2) Incident severity definitions (quick reference)
- Sev-0 (SevZero): Full production outage or data loss impacting >95% of requests or all customers. Immediate page and company-wide comms.
- Sev-1: Severe degradation (large % increase in latency/errors) affecting many customers or major features. Requires extended on-call engagement.
- Sev-2: Partial degradation or localized outage affecting subset of customers, degraded performance under SLOs.
- Sev-3: Minor operational issues, non-urgent bugs, maintenance windows, or internal-only impacts.

3) Detection and Alerting
- Alert sources: Prometheus SLO alerts, runtime error-rate alarms, latency P95/P99 thresholds, customer reports (support tickets/CS), automated canary failures, status-page monitoring.
- Standard thresholds (examples):
  - API error-rate: >1.5% sustained over 2 min => Sev-1 candidate.
  - Request latency P95 > 600ms on hosted API for 2 min => Sev-1 candidate.
  - Model KV cache miss rate spiking 3x baseline => investigate performance regressions.
- First responder obligation: Acknowledge the pager within 5 minutes and set an incident channel.

4) Triage and initial play (first 15 minutes)
1. Acknowledge and join the incident bridge (Zoom/Google Meet) and create a dedicated Slack channel #inc-<short-id>.
2. Capture quick facts: start time, symptoms, affected services/regions, initial severity, paging list.
3. Assign roles (see section 6): Incident Commander (IC), Communications Lead, SRE lead, Product/Engineering L1 owner, Customer Success liaison.
4. Start a running timeline and hypothesis list in the incident channel.
5. Begin mitigation steps from the relevant runbook; if no runbook exists, escalate to platform on-call.

5) Roles and responsibilities
- Incident Commander (IC): overall decision-maker for incident triage and business impact assessment. Coordinates resources and declares severity.
- Communications Lead: owns internal and external messaging cadence (see templates), status page updates, and customer-facing comms.
- SRE/Platform Lead: leads infrastructure diagnosis, capacity/failover actions, and rollback decisions.
- Service/Model Owner: leads application/model-level debugging and configuration changes.
- Postmortem Author: appointed post-incident to collect timeline, facts, and follow-ups.

6) On-call rotations and escalation policy
- Primary on-call (weekly rotation) for platform and each service team; secondary on-call for escalation (2-3 week rotation for secondaries).
- Paging order: primary -> secondary -> team lead -> Eng SRE on-call -> Engineering Director.
- On-call expectations: carry pager, respond within 5 minutes, be able to join a call and perform initial mitigation.
- Handoffs: daily stand-up handoff message in #oncall-handoffs with current incidents, outstanding actions, and follow-ups. Formal handoff document required for shift >8 hours.

7) Runbook structure and examples
- Runbook template (each runbook must include): Purpose; Preconditions (what triggers use); Observable symptoms & key metrics; Step-by-step Mitigation (numbered); Validation steps; Rollback criteria; Owner and last-tested date; Runbook playbook commands and sample queries.

Example: Hosted API 5xx Spike runbook- Purpose: Mitigate sustained 5xx spike on Redwood hosted inference API.- Preconditions: API error-rate > 1.5% for 2 min or P95 spikes to >1s.- Observables: error-rate metric, upstream model-runtime errors, GPU OOM events, autoscaler events, routing error logs.- Mitigation steps:
  1) IC: Add "incident: hosted-api-5xx" label and set severity.
  2) SRE: Check region-level instance health dashboard (dashboards-and-alerts -> hosted-api).
  3) SRE: Run: kubectl get pods -n hosted-api -o wide | grep CrashLoopBackOff; if pods in CrashLoopBackOff, scale down and restart: kubectl rollout restart deployment/hosted-api -n hosted-api.
  4) Platform: Inspect model-variant logs for OOM: rlog query 'oom' --last 15m --service hosted-runtime. If OOMs, temporarily revert to a lower-memory model variant or trigger burst to Dedicated capacity.
  5) If autoscaler flapping: pause autoscaler: curl -X POST https://internal-api/autoscaler/pause -d '{"reason":"inc-hosted-5xx"}'.
  6) Communications Lead: Post status page initial message and internal summary.
  7) Validate: Confirm error-rate dropping < 0.5% for 5 consecutive minutes and latency returning near baseline.
  8) If no improvement in 20 minutes, escalate to cross-team war-room and consider traffic shielding by routing to redundant region.

8) Postmortem and RCA requirements
- Trigger: Any Sev-1 or Sev-0 incident must have a postmortem within 72 hours (initial draft) and a final postmortem within 14 days.
- Postmortem must include: timeline with timestamps, impact (customers, duration, SLO breach), root cause analysis, detection and mitigation steps, action items with owners and deadlines, risk assessment, and verification plan.
- Postmortem review: at least one technical reviewer and one CS/business reviewer. Postmortems are published internally and linked to the related incident ticket.

9) Communications: templates & cadence
- Cadence: Initial public status update within 30 minutes for Sev-0/Sev-1 (or earlier if customer-notified through CS). Internal updates every 15 minutes during active remediation. Customer-facing updates every 60 minutes for prolonged incidents until resolved.

Status page template (public):
- Title: Redwood Inference — Incident: <short-description>
- Impact: Brief summary of affected services/regions.
- Status: Identified / Investigating / Mitigating / Monitoring / Resolved.
- Latest update (timestamp): short bullet of progress.
- Next update ETA: HH:MM UTC.
- Affected customers: (opt) list of named customers if notified.
- Mitigation in progress: brief bulleted list.
- Contact: support@redwoodinference.com and link to status RSS.

Customer email template (initial, for Sev-1/Sev-0):
Subject: Redwood Inference — Issue impacting <service> (Incident <id>)
Hello <Customer Name>,
We are investigating an issue affecting <service> that may impact your requests. We have identified the symptoms as <short summary> and are actively working on mitigation. Our current status: Investigating.
What we are doing: <short bullets of mitigation steps>.
Estimated next update: <time>.
We apologize for the disruption. If you are experiencing urgent business impact, please reply to this email or contact your CS rep.
— Redwood Inference Support Team

Customer update template (follow-up):
Subject: Update on Incident <id>: <short state>
Hello <Customer Name>,
Update: <state the progress and any workarounds>.
Estimated resolution: <ETA or N/A>.
Action for customers: <suggested steps if any>.
We will follow up again at <time>.

Post-resolution customer summary:
Subject: Incident <id> resolved — <short impact summary>
Hello <Customer Name>,
The incident has been resolved at <timestamp> UTC. Root cause: <short root cause>. Impact: <what customers experienced>. Actions taken: <high level remediation and permanent fix plan>. Next steps: <planned follow-ups, timeline for fixes>.
Contact: Your CS rep or support@redwoodinference.com

10) Game days and testing
- Purpose: Validate runbooks, rotation responsiveness, SLO monitoring, and customer comms practice.
- Frequency: Quarterly cross-team game days; targeted exercises before major releases.
- Format: Pre-announced functional drills and occasional surprise drills for rotations. Each game day must have a facilitator and observer who fills a Game Day report.
- Game day checklist:
  - Confirm synthetic traffic and canary alarms are active.
  - Simulate incident (e.g., model OOM, network partition, autoscaler failure).
  - Execute runbooks and run communications cadence.
  - Capture timings: detection -> mitigation -> resolution.
  - Post-game postmortem and runbook updates within 7 days.

11) Training and runbook testing cadence
- Each runbook must be exercised at least once per 6 months by relevant owners.
- New service teams must complete an on-call readiness checklist and shadow rotation for two cycles.

12) Metrics and SLOs to monitor in incidents
- Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly for hosted inference API (tracked by success-rate).
- Latency SLO: P95 < 300ms for standard hosted requests.
- Error budget burn alerts: page when 50% monthly error budget consumed and again at 80%.
- Post-incident metrics: time-to-detect (TTD), time-to-mitigate (TTM), time-to-resolve (TTR), customer impact minutes.

13) Escalation matrix and contacts
- Primary on-call: paged via PagerDuty (see internal roster).
- Secondary on-call: paged if primary does not acknowledge within 10 minutes.
- SRE manager and Eng Director contacts listed in internal roster (linked in related_pages).

14) Documentation hygiene and ownership
- Every runbook must declare: owner, last_tested_date, and next_review_date. Reviews are on a 6-month cadence.
- Runbook naming: service-runbook-<short-name>-YYYYMM (e.g., hosted-api-5xx-202602).

15) Post-incident verification and closure
- Validation: Confirm metrics are back within baseline for at least two full measurement windows (10-15 minutes each).
- Action items: tracked in Jira with owner and due date; must include verification steps.
- Closure: IC signs off and documents closure in incident channel and status page; postmortem linked and published.

Appendices
A) Useful CLI snippets and queries
- Check API pods: kubectl get pods -n hosted-api -l app=hosted-api -o wide
- Tail logs for model runtime: rlog tail hosted-runtime --since 30m
- Query error-rate: promql: sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))

B) Example postmortem outline (to paste into template)
- Title: Incident <id> — <short description>
- Severity:
- Timeline:
- Impact:
- Root cause:
- Detection and mitigation actions:
- Corrective actions / action items (owner + due date):
- Verification plan:
- Lessons learned:

C) Runbook maintenance log (example table text)
- | Runbook | Owner | Last tested | Next review | Notes |
- | hosted-api-5xx | Platform SRE | 2026-01-18 | 2026-07-18 | added autoscaler pause step |

D) Quick links
- Incident ticket template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-ticket-template
- PagerDuty roster: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/pagerduty-roster
- Dashboards: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts

If you own a runbook referenced here and it is not up-to-date, please update immediately and add a last-tested date. For questions or to schedule a game day, contact the Eng SRE team or drop a message in #eng-sre.
